projects.name: Geelong Fast Rail
projects.description: Reduces Melbourne–Geelong travel time to under 30 minutes. State Government committed. Transformational for property values along the corridor.

projects.name: Armstrong Creek Growth Corridor
projects.description: Master-planned precinct delivering 50,000 new residents, retail, schools, and employment across 6,400 ha south of Geelong.

projects.name: NDIA National HQ
projects.description: The National Disability Insurance Agency established its national headquarters in Geelong — bringing 1,600 high-quality government jobs to the region permanently.

projects.name: Geelong Convention & Exhibition Centre
projects.description: Waterfront expansion positioning Geelong as a major events and business destination. Drives hospitality employment and tourism spend.

profileTags: Capital city proximity without capital city pricing
Established inner-ring pockets with genuine scarcity

risks.title: Fast Rail timeline uncertainty
risks.description: The Geelong Fast Rail remains a State Government commitment without a confirmed completion date. Political changes could delay or alter scope. The growth case holds without it, but the Fast Rail is a significant upside catalyst — not a guarantee.

risks.title: Interest rate sensitivity
risks.description: Like most regional markets, Geelong buyers are more rate-sensitive than inner-city markets. A sustained rate environment above 5.5% could soften demand from owner-occupiers, slowing price growth in the short term.

risks.title: Armstrong Creek supply
risks.description: The Armstrong Creek growth corridor is adding significant new housing stock. This can suppress rental yields and price growth in the outer-ring new-build segments. Established inner-ring properties are largely insulated from this supply pressure.

triggers: Fast Rail funding confirmed or timeline firmed
